Adding a site

\n\n
    \n
  1. Open the Browser and navigate to the site.
    2. \n
  2. Click ⋯ in the toolbar.
    3. \n
  3. Choose Add Site to Dock.
    4. \n
\n\n \n\n

The site appears in the dock with its own icon, taken from the site's own favicon. Click it and it opens in a dedicated window with no tab strip and no address bar, just the site.

\n\n \n\n

Rearranging and customising

\n\n

Right-click any dock item for its options, rename it, give it a different icon, move it, or remove it.

\n\n \n\n

Two useful distinctions when removing something:

\n\n
    \n
  • Hide from dock, takes the tile away but keeps the site installed.
    • \n
  • Uninstall Site, removes it entirely.
    • \n
\n\n

Built-in apps you never use can be hidden the same way, and everything can be dragged into whatever order you like. Dock size, magnification and auto-hide live in Settings › Dock.

\n\n \n\n

The Apps drawer

\n\n

The first tile in the dock opens the Apps drawer: everything installed, in one grid, with a search box. Handy when you've installed more sites than fit comfortably in the dock.

\n\n \n\n

Sites are managed from their own icon here, right-click one in the drawer for the same rename, re-icon, hide and uninstall options.

\n\n

Floating windows and detached tabs

\n\n

Any browser tab can become a window of its own: right-click the tab and choose Open in Floating Window. That window is independent, move it, resize it, put it full screen, which is how you get a video playing on one part of the screen while you work on another.

\n\n

An installed site can also be set to open as a floating window by default, so clicking its dock icon goes straight there.

\n\n

Finding things fast

\n\n

Press Option Space for the search overlay. It searches your apps, your installed sites, your files across mounted locations, and will run a web search for anything else you type.

\n\n \n\n

To see everything currently open, press Ctrl ↑ (Option ↑ on iPad) for the overview, or hold Ctrl and press Tab to cycle windows.

\n\n \n\n

Your session comes back

\n\n

Windows you leave open, including installed sites and detached tabs, reopen at the same size and position next time you plug in a display. So does your place on the page. Setting the desktop up the way you like it is a one-time job.

\n\n
\n

XeOS: External Display Browser turns an iPhone or iPad into a full desktop on any monitor, TV or projector.

\n

\n\n
\n

Common questions

\n\n

Are installed sites separate from the browser's tabs?

\n

Yes, each gets its own window. They share your logins and site data, so you don't sign in twice.

\n\n

Can I change an installed site's icon?

\n

Yes. Right-click it in the dock or the Apps drawer and set a custom icon and name.

\n\n

How do I get a built-in app back after hiding it?

\n

Settings › Dock lists the built-in apps and lets you show them again.

\n\n

Can I pin a folder to the dock too?

\n

Yes, right-click a folder in the Files sidebar and choose Pin to Dock.
